settings.meta_1: Ada Ferrer · independent web & AI developer
settings.heading: I build it.
settings.subheading: Front-end and AI builds for design studios, when the concept is hard to ship.
settings.lead: Turning difficult designs into fast, stable websites since 2011. These days the toolkit includes AI.

settings.text: Studios bring the concept. I make sure it survives production. If an uneven grid is what makes a page feel alive, I change the code to fit the grid, not the other way round.

settings.label: [02] Selected projects
settings.note: Field notes · client names kept private
settings.intro: Most client work is under NDA. So each case shows how it was built rather than who it was for.

settings.title: A shop site built on one angle
settings.text: Every slanted edge on the site uses the 22° angle from the store's shelving, from the wide desktop layout down to the phone. The slider shows a hint of the next colour just before it changes.

settings.title: Product photos that name themselves
settings.text: Search data and an image model decide how each product photo is named, described and tagged. Several hundred photos a day go through it, and nobody renames files by hand any more.

settings.title: An outdoor guide you can tilt
settings.text: Routes drawn on a live 3D relief, with pages that load in under a second on hotel wifi. Lighthouse on mobile: 97 on the home page and 99 on route pages.

settings.title: Websites for studios
settings.text: Motion-rich sites and CMS builds, made side by side with your designers and handed over so your team can run them.

settings.title: AI for your team
settings.text: Practical workshops on coding assistants, then the small tools and workflows your team actually needs, plus a plain list of what not to automate.

settings.title: AI inside products
settings.text: Assistants and search that answer from your client's own content, tested on real user questions and showing their sources.

settings.label: [04] Working with studios
settings.note: Quiet by default · white-label on request
settings.heading: Your design on the surface. My code underneath.

settings.title: Brief
settings.text: A call, your deck and the limits. I come back with questions and a first sense of scope.

settings.title: Prototype
settings.text: The hardest interaction runs in a browser before anyone gets attached to a static mock-up.

settings.title: Build
settings.text: A staging link from day one and a written log of decisions. No surprise reveal at the end.

settings.title: Handover
settings.text: Docs, a short CMS session for your team and a tidy repository.
